title: TikTok Ads Help: content disclosure setting for creators
supports: Posts promoting a brand, product or service must have the content disclosure setting on; legal requirements vary by country and the US FTC Endorsement Guides apply

title: TikTok Ads Help: video play metrics
supports: Video views count playback starts with replays excluded; average play time includes replays; 'video views at 100%' counts full-length plays
limit: Ads-side definitions, last updated November 2025; creator-account analytics screens use different terms and may not match; no metric named total play time or completion rate on this page

title: TikTok Integrity and Authenticity policy
supports: Bulk or automated engagement, bots and trading in artificial engagement are prohibited; manipulative engagement bait can lose For You eligibility
limit: Page body could not be fetched directly; wording is from search extracts of this page, which was labelled as the May 2024 version; a newer guideline set may exist, so read the live page before relying on exact text

title: Meta Help: differences between Page views, reach and impressions
supports: Page views count profile views; reach is an estimated count of people who saw content from or about the Page; impressions count times content entered a person's screen
limit: Page is undated; it does not define Views, which Meta announced as replacing impressions for non-video content, so check the current metric names in the Insights export you actually use; Ads Manager definitions differ

title: Meta Transparency Center: Spam Community Standard
supports: Buying, selling or exchanging engagement, posting or creating assets at very high frequencies manually or automatically, and links that promise different content than they deliver are prohibited
limit: Change log runs to Jun 27, 2024 plus an undated current entry, so the live text may be newer; Groups and Pages may add their own rules

title: Meta Business Help: paid partnership labels and branded content
supports: Branded content for a business partner needs the Paid Partnership label; promoting your own product is not branded content but may still need disclosing, and legal disclosure duties remain with the poster
limit: Page body could not be fetched directly; wording is from search extracts of Meta's Business Help pages, which are undated; confirm in Meta's current policy before relying on exact text

title: X Developer Policy
supports: API bot accounts must say what they are and who runs them; using the API for spam or platform manipulation is prohibited; no bulk, aggressive or spammy actions; get explicit consent before automated replies or direct messages and honour opt-outs
limit: Page carries no date and says it may change without notice; it defers to separate Automation Rules for detail that I could not fetch

title: X API metrics documentation
supports: Impressions count times a post appeared on a user's screen and are not unique; non-public, organic and promoted metrics are only available for posts from the last 30 days
limit: API-side definitions; the page did not define engagements or link clicks in the text I read, and the X Ads export defines engagements and impressions differently, so copy the label you actually exported

title: X Help: Authenticity (platform manipulation and spam)
supports: Inauthentic accounts, bulk or unsolicited replies and mentions, engagement trading schemes and follow churn are prohibited; limits on running multiple accounts
limit: help.x.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches; wording is from search extracts, one dated April 2025; confirm the live page before relying on exact text

title: LinkedIn Professional Community Policies
supports: Do not use invitations to send promotional messages to people you do not know; untargeted, unwanted, gratuitously repetitive promotional messages and artificially increasing engagement are prohibited
limit: Page states no effective date; spam rules are general, and the explicit ban on automation tools sits in the separate Help Center page and the User Agreement

title: LinkedIn Help: prohibited software and extensions
supports: Crawlers, bots and browser extensions that scrape, modify or automate activity on LinkedIn, and fake accounts or fake engagement, are not allowed; members risk restriction or shutdown
limit: Help Center page is undated; it describes consequences in general terms and does not list every tool

title: LinkedIn Help: content analytics for your Page
supports: Impressions count times a post was shown, with 300 milliseconds and half the post on screen, as an estimate; members reached counts distinct members without repeat displays; clicks exclude reactions, comments and reposts; click-through rate is clicks divided by impressions
limit: Page shows Last updated 1 year ago; it counts clicks inside engagements, while LinkedIn's separate post analytics page leaves clicks out of engagements, and Campaign Manager defines engagement rate again, so state which page and period you used

title: Steamworks Documentation: wishlist reporting
supports: The reports portal tracks wishlist additions, purchases and deletions; data is refreshed daily for the previous date; the CSV has DateLocal and MonthCohort columns; platform breakdowns reflect only players who set a platform preference
limit: The page does not define additions or deletions precisely or state accuracy; the latest day is always excluded; a web API with wishlist_adds, wishlist_deletes and wishlist_purchases fields is known only from search extracts

title: Steamworks Documentation: UTM analytics
supports: Tracked visits are visits to the product page by users logged in to Steam; wishlist, purchase and activation conversions count only within 72 hours of the UTM click; links must point to an app or sale page and include utm_source or utm_campaign
limit: Only signed-in visitors are counted, so tracked visits and conversions are a lower bound on real traffic; abnormal-behaviour visits are excluded without detail

title: Steamworks Documentation: advertising on Steam
supports: Steam contains no paid advertising; developers may run paid campaigns outside Steam to drive traffic to their product pages, and Valve suggests Store Widgets and UTM Analytics for them
limit: Page is undated and says nothing about the effectiveness or cost of any off-Steam channel

title: Steamworks: Steam Direct onboarding
supports: $100 non-refundable fee per product, recoupable after $1,000 adjusted gross revenue; bank, tax and identity verification; 1-5 day review; 30 days after paying before the first release; a public coming-soon page for at least two weeks before release
limit: Page gives no calendar dates; fee and waiting periods can change, so confirm them in Steamworks before paying
